title: Single-photon controlled phase shifts with colloidal quantum dots at room temperature
source_used: Science Advances (abstract and author list via Crossref API, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aee1340)
key_facts: Paper in Science Advances (volume 12, issue 40), listed 2 Oct 2026, by six authors at the Institute of Semiconductors, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing (two also at the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences).
The team placed a single colloidal quantum dot (a tiny crystal made in liquid) onto a photonic crystal hybrid microcavity (a structure that traps light) using a soft nanoprobe technique.
They studied strong coupling between the quantum dot and bound states in the continuum in the cavity.
They measured wavelength- and power-dependent phase shifts with photoluminescence spectroscopy, Michelson interferometry and continuous-wave pump-probe methods.
Controlled pi-phase shifts of a single photon were demonstrated, both with a single quantum dot and with a high concentration of quantum dots coupled to the cavity.
The authors say the work gives an experimental basis for room-temperature quantum optoelectronic devices, including quantum phase gates and ultralow-power optical switches.
Funding named: National Natural Science Foundation of China and a Chinese national quantum science major project.
quote_evidence: Controlled π-phase shifts of a single photon were experimentally demonstrated in both single colloidal quantum dot and high-concentration colloidal quantum dots coupled microcavity systems.
This work provides an experimental basis for the development of room temperature quantum optoelectronic devices, including quantum phase gates and ultralow power optical switches.
why_it_matters_hint: A basic quantum logic ingredient (a controlled phase shift of one photon) was shown without deep cooling, but only as a laboratory experiment.
event_date: Published in Science Advances on 2 Oct 2026; experiments done before publication (dates not stated in the abstract).
